text: Shephatiah son of Mattan, Gedaliah son of Pashhur, Jucal son of Shelemiah, and Pashhur son of Malchiah heard the words Jeremiah was speaking to all the people:
"This is what the LORD says: Whoever stays in this city will die by the sword, by famine, or by plague, but whoever goes out to the Chaldeans will live; he will escape with his life and survive.
This is what the LORD says: This city will surely be handed over to the army of the king of Babylon, and he will capture it."

So the officials said to the king, "This man must be put to death. By speaking such words to them he is undermining the courage of the soldiers who are left in this city and of all the people. This man is not seeking the welfare of this people, but their ruin."
King Zedekiah answered, "He is in your hands; the king can do nothing to stop you."

So they took Jeremiah and threw him into the cistern of Malchiah the king's son, which was in the courtyard of the guard. They lowered Jeremiah by ropes. There was no water in the cistern, only mud, and Jeremiah sank into the mud.
But Ebed-melech the Cushite, a court official in the king's palace, heard that they had put Jeremiah into the cistern. While the king was sitting in the Benjamin Gate,
Ebed-melech left the palace and said to him,

"My lord the king, these men have done wrong in all they have done to Jeremiah the prophet. They have thrown him into the cistern, where he will starve to death, since there is no more bread in the city."
Then the king commanded Ebed-melech the Cushite, "Take thirty men with you from here and lift Jeremiah the prophet out of the cistern before he dies."

versions.text: Then the king commanded Ebed-melech the Cushite, "Take thirty men with you and lift Jeremiah the prophet out of the cistern before he dies."
versions.explanation: The Hebrew includes מִזֶּה ("from here"), indicating the men were to be taken from where the king was; the omission slightly reduces the concreteness of the command.

text: So Ebed-melech took the men with him and went to a room beneath the treasury in the palace. From there he took worn-out rags and cast-off clothing and let them down with ropes to Jeremiah in the cistern.
Ebed-melech the Cushite called down to Jeremiah, "Put these rags and cast-off clothing under your armpits, to pad the ropes." Jeremiah did so,
and they pulled him up by the ropes and lifted him out of the cistern. And Jeremiah remained in the courtyard of the guard.
Then King Zedekiah sent for Jeremiah the prophet and had him brought to the third entrance of the LORD's house. "I am going to ask you something," the king said. "Hide nothing from me."
Jeremiah said to Zedekiah, "If I tell you, you will surely put me to death. And if I give you advice, you will not listen to me."
But King Zedekiah swore to Jeremiah in private, "As surely as the LORD lives, who gave us breath, I will not put you to death or hand you over to those men who want to kill you."

Then Jeremiah said to Zedekiah, "This is what the LORD, the God of hosts, the God of Israel, says: If you will surrender to the officers of the king of Babylon, your life will be spared, this city will not be burned down, and you and your household will live.
But if you will not surrender to the officers of the king of Babylon, this city will be handed over to the Chaldeans; they will burn it down, and you yourself will not escape their hands."
King Zedekiah said to Jeremiah, "I am afraid of the Jews who have gone over to the Chaldeans; they may hand me over to them, and they will abuse me."
"They will not hand you over," Jeremiah replied. "Obey the voice of the LORD in what I am telling you. Then it will go well with you, and your life will be spared.
But if you refuse to surrender, this is what the LORD has shown me:

All the women left in the palace of the king of Judah will be led out to the officers of the king of Babylon, and they will say to you: 'Your trusted friends misled you and got the better of you. Now that your feet are sunk in the mire, they have turned their backs on you.'

All your wives and children will be led out to the Chaldeans, and you yourself will not escape their hands. You will be captured by the king of Babylon, and because of you this city will be burned down."

versions.text: All your wives and children will be led out to the Chaldeans, and you yourself will not escape their hands. You will be captured by the king of Babylon, and this city will be burned down."
versions.explanation: The Hebrew verb תִּשְׂרֹף is second person masculine singular ("you will burn this city with fire"), placing responsibility on Zedekiah; the passive rendering loses this. If the passive is retained for readability, a footnote noting the literal Hebrew ("you will burn this city with fire") would be helpful.

text: Then Zedekiah said to Jeremiah, "Let no one know about this conversation, or you may die.
If the officials hear that I have spoken with you and they come and say, 'Tell us what you said to the king and what the king said to you. Do not hide it from us, or we will kill you'—
then tell them, 'I was pleading with the king not to send me back to Jonathan's house to die there.'"
All the officials did come to Jeremiah and question him, and he told them exactly what the king had ordered him to say. So they said no more to him, for no one had overheard the conversation.
